mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate level increases the risk-free rate component of equity discount rates, reducing the present value of future cash flows and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day returns is negative but statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes economic contraction and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by > 0.3pp over 3 months, or the average return in such instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates contraction in the housing sector and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST falls and FEDFUNDS rises, or the average return in such instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve maintains restrictive monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 5.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high level of total employment (PAYEMS) indicates strong labor market conditions supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. This mechanism is always active.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 135,000 (thousands), or the correlation between PAYEMS level and 5-day returns is positive but statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level below 1400.0 thousand units signals weak consumer demand for housing, correlating with broader economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST is below 1400.0, or the average return in such instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates contraction in manufacturing and construction sectors, reducing economic output and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO and HOUST both decline, or the average return in such instances is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high consumer spending regimes (RSAFS > 350,000 million dollars), strong residential sales activity supports economic growth and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 350,000, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
